title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #475: Graham's Rearrangement Conjecture**

Given a non-zero subset A of 𝔽ₚ, can we always arrange it as a₁, ..., aₜ so all partial sums are distinct?

**Status:** OPEN in general; proven for various ranges of t.

This is a fundamental problem in additive combinatorics, connecting prime fields, sequencing, and partial sums.

title: Partial Sums and Valid Orderings
content:
**partialSums l:** The sequence of cumulative sums of a list l, computed via List.scanl.

**IsValidOrdering A ordering:** An ordering of A is valid if:
1. The ordering contains exactly the elements of A (no duplicates, same set)
2. All partial sums are distinct (no collisions in 𝔽ₚ)

**GrahamConjecture p:** For prime p, every non-zero subset of 𝔽ₚ has a valid ordering.

title: Small Cases: t ≤ 12 (Costa-Pellegrini 2020)
content:
**costa_pellegrini_2020 (axiom):** For |A| ≤ 12, valid orderings exist.

Verified through a combination of exhaustive computation and theoretical reductions. Costa and Pellegrini (2020) established this systematically.

**small_sets_have_valid_orderings (proved):** Derives the result by instantiating the axiom.

title: Large Cases: t ≥ p - 3
content:
**hicks_ollis_schmitt_2019 (axiom):** For sets of size p - 3, p - 2, or p - 1, valid orderings exist. When A is almost all of 𝔽ₚ \ {0}, structural arguments suffice.

**graham_full_set (axiom):** Graham originally proved the t = p - 1 case constructively, providing an explicit algorithm to produce a valid ordering.

title: Logarithmic Range (Kravitz 2024)
content:
**kravitz_2024 (axiom):** For |A| ≤ log p / log log p, valid orderings exist.

Kravitz (2024) proved this, and Will Sawin independently observed the same bound on MathOverflow. This significantly extends beyond the constant bound of 12, though log p / log log p grows slowly.

title: Beyond the Rectification Barrier (Bedert-Kravitz 2024)
content:
**bedert_kravitz_2024 (axiom):** For |A| ≤ exp((log p)^{1/4}), valid orderings exist.

This is a major breakthrough. The 'rectification barrier' at log p / log log p was a technical obstacle that limited all previous methods. Bedert and Kravitz (2024) developed fundamentally new techniques to go far beyond.

exp((log p)^{1/4}) grows much faster than log p / log log p, representing a substantial improvement.

title: Alspach's Conjecture and Equivalence
content:
**AlspachConjecture G:** For any finite abelian group G, every non-zero subset has a valid ordering. This generalizes Graham's conjecture from 𝔽ₚ to all abelian groups.

**graham_is_alspach_for_prime_field (proved):** Graham's conjecture is exactly Alspach's conjecture for G = 𝔽ₚ. The proof is by direct unfolding of definitions.

title: Constructive vs Existential Proofs
content:
**HasExplicitValidOrdering A:** There exists a function that computes a valid ordering for A.

**graham_constructive (axiom):** Graham's proof for the full non-zero set was constructive, giving an explicit algorithm.

Some proofs are constructive (giving explicit orderings), others are existential (proving one exists without constructing it).

title: Summary Theorem
content:
**erdos_475_summary (proved from axioms):**

Combines the three main verified ranges:
1. **Small t ≤ 12:** Costa-Pellegrini 2020
2. **Large t ≥ p - 3:** Hicks-Ollis-Schmitt 2019
3. **Medium t ≤ exp((log p)^{1/4}):** Bedert-Kravitz 2024

Proved by: `⟨costa_pellegrini_2020 p hp12, hicks_ollis_schmitt_2019 p, bedert_kravitz_2024 p hp2⟩`

The general conjecture for arbitrary t remains OPEN.
